exposure: Maternal obesity (classified into Class I: BMI 30-34.9, Class II: BMI 35-39.9, Class III: BMI >=40)
cohort: The study included 512 pregnant women with obesity who delivered at Dr. Soetomo General Hospital and Airlangga University Hospital Surabaya in 2023.
finding: Significant differences were observed in maternal outcomes of preeclampsia, eclampsia, and mode of delivery, as well as perinatal outcomes of macrosomia and NICU admission, across the three obesity classes.
mod_finding: There were significant differences observed in the mode of delivery (specifically, 53.3% delivered by cesarean section overall) across the three obesity classes.
